course_name_original: Soldadura y Otras Tecnologías de Unión

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to identify problems associated with welded joints and to make decisions that ensure their integrity and good performance.
Ability to select the most suitable joining technology depending on the type of material and the specific application required.

Ability to select the most suitable welding process and adjust its characteristic parameters in order to obtain a quality welded joint, both from a metallurgical, mechanical, and economic point of view.
Ability to design and calculate an optimal welded joint, considering the various factors involved.
Ability to handle the regulations and the scientific-technical equipment necessary to carry out the metallurgical and mechanical characterization of welded joints.
Ability to carry out quality control of a welded structure, scientifically analyzing possible failures and proposing solutions to them.
Ability to delve into the analysis of a specific scientific-technological problem, analyze it, identify the problem and provide a proposed solution.
Ability to communicate orally and in writing and to prepare and subsequently publicly defend a research paper on a specific problem.
Ability to manage different resources and technologies that allow obtaining updated scientific information on the research topic to be developed.
Ability to organize a specific job and carry it out in a group.
Know the different joining technologies as well as their specific characteristics and their suitability for use depending on different variables.
Know how the welding process modifies the microstructure and mechanical behavior of materials.
Know how to optimize a welded joint through improving its design and subsequent calculation.
Know how quality control is carried out in welding, attending to the most widely used international standards.
Know the existing standardized tests to characterize the mechanical behavior of welded joints.
Select the most suitable joining technology depending on the type of material and the specific application required.
Select the most suitable welding process and adjust its characteristic parameters in order to obtain a quality welded joint, both from a metallurgical, mechanical, and economic point of view.
Design and calculate an optimal welded joint, considering the various factors involved.
Handle the scientific-technical equipment necessary to carry out the metallurgical and mechanical characterization of welded joints in accordance with the most used standards.
Carry out complete quality control of a welded structure, scientifically analyzing possible failures and proposing solutions to them.
Organize a specific job and carry it out in a group.
Write a scientific paper concisely and present it orally with clarity.
Create research interest in the student.
Provide the student with an organizational sense for group work.
Formation of an open, critical and entrepreneurial spirit.

syllabus_topics: Main joining technologies. Riveted and bolted joints. Adhesive joints. Welded joints: Continuity, advantages and disadvantages. Types of joints and nomenclature used in welding. Nomenclature used in welding.
Most commonly used welding processes industrially. Shielded metal arc welding. Semi-automatic welding. Submerged arc welding. Laser welding. Resistance welding. Other welding techniques.

Welding thermal cycle. General characteristics. Factors affecting the welding thermal cycle: type of material to be welded, thickness and size of the parts, joint geometry, heat input, preheating and post-heating, welding procedure, operational technique.
Zones of the welded joint. Welding metallurgy. The fusion zone: dilution phenomena. The heat affected zone (HAZ): Transformations during heating and during cooling. Parts of the HAZ.
Thermal stresses and cracking. Stresses and deformations due to the welding thermal cycle: Measures to minimize them. Hot cracking and cold cracking. Lamellar tearing. Post-weld heat treatment.

Weldability of steels and other metal alloys. Definition of metallurgical weldability. Influencing factors. Weldability of low and medium alloy steels. Weldability of stainless steels. Weldability of other metal alloys.
Microstructures and defects in the welded joint. Metallography of the welded joint. Typical microstructures of the different zones. Typical defects of the different zones of the welded joint.
Mechanical behavior of welded joints. Most commonly used mechanical tests in the characterization of welded joints: tension, hardness, bending, impact, fracture and fatigue. Standards.
Design and calculation of welded joints under static load. Factors influencing the choice of joint type. Design and calculation of joints under static load. Examples.
Design and calculation of welded joints under fatigue loads. Factors influencing the choice of joint type. Detail categories. Examples.
Specification and qualification of welded joints and welders. Quality control in welding. Specification of a welding procedure. Qualification of welded joints and welders. Standards.
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices using machines and equipment for welded joints
Review of experimental methodology for specific tests (mechanical tests, microstructural analysis, defect analysis)

assessment_methods.method: Completion and submission of exercises and laboratory practice scripts
Group or individual work presentation and discussion

assessment_rules: Student learning will be continuously evaluated throughout the course. The overall evaluation of submitted exercises and laboratory practice scripts accounts for 20% of the final grade. Two written tests will be conducted at the end of the course: one for practical exercises (30%) and one for theoretical questions (30%). A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required in the combined score of these two written tests to pass the course. The remaining 20% of the final grade will correspond to the evaluation of individual or group work, which will be publicly presented and debated.
